source.note: Measured on the working tree of branch work/2026-11-12 (tool uncommitted at measurement time); engine code unchanged.

conditions_note: Busy processes are Node loops at normal priority; 16 saturates all logical CPUs. One unrecorded warm-up per case; warm file cache. Windows 11 unpacked development layout (desktop/runtime), not an installer, portable executable or clean machine.
additional_observation: An earlier 16-busy-process attempt (first version of the tool, 10 runs) aborted when the 5 s hello deadline expired and the client reported ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE; the three later 16-process runs completed with ready 1.2-1.4 s. Saturated-CPU behaviour is therefore intermittent, not a stable pass.

gates_against_m8_1.cold_ready_5s_from_spawn_through_hello: idle: verify 2.1 s + ready 0.31 s (about 2.5 s) passes; 16 busy: verify median 16.0 s (max 27.1 s) fails; this is verification plus spawn, a conservative reading of the gate
gates_against_m8_1.kill_terminal_within_2s: after the change: passes idle (5 ms) and saturated (29 ms median, 33 ms max); before it: 1.7 s idle, 2.6 s saturated
gates_against_m8_1.process_and_scratch_cleanup: no leftover runtime process or scratch directory in any measured run, after orderly stop and forced kill

after_forced_kill_change.change: Forced termination now ends the coordinator immediately (child.kill) and the coordinator joins a kill-on-close Job Object (src/sedcoretool/engine/lifetime.py) so its workers die with it; taskkill /T remains only as a backstop. Authorised by the maintainer on 12 November 2026. Runtime rebuilt before measuring.
after_forced_kill_change.result: Forced kill: idle 1707 ms -> 5 ms median; 16 busy 2619 ms -> 29 ms median. No leftover process or scratch directory. Verification under 16 busy processes is unchanged (median about 20 s, max 38.5 s) and still fails the 5 s gate; it is CPU-bound hashing and is left for a maintainer policy decision.
